successors.name: Maya city-states (Postclassic)
successors.text: the northern lowlands and the central Peten that Cliopatria keeps in its 850 shape

ledger.x: -300: the cities of the Mirador Basin (El Mirador, Nakbe, El Tintal) rise as the first large Maya centres.
About 150: the Mirador Basin is abandoned.
849: the southern kingdoms drop out of the Maya envelope.
849: the Classic Maya city-state envelope ends and the northern Postclassic row takes over.

wars.name: Intervention of Teotihuacan at Tikal
wars.outcome: In January 378 Siyaj K'ak' arrived from the west, the Tikal king Chak Tok Ich'aak died the same day and a Teotihuacan-linked ruler followed; no territory is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Tikal-Calakmul hegemonic wars
wars.outcome: Calakmul and Caracol defeated Tikal in 562 ('Sky Witness defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king'); Tikal's Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeated Calakmul in August 695.

certainty.note: No Maya state had a surveyed or treaty border; the envelope is a culture-area outline and every kingdom's reach is approximate.
